title: One number for all your agents

steps.text: Tomorrow at nine, I demo to Northwind, our biggest prospect. Tonight, I fly to New York. Three agents are working for me: Claude Code on a checkout bug, ChatGPT on our Slack, and Gemini on my email and calendar.
But the moment I leave my desk, they're stuck. Claude Code has a question, and it just waits.
Today, all it can do is send a notification. I see it an hour later, and the work just sat there.
I need one number that runs all my agents, and calls me when they need me.
{{product}} is my own agent, with one phone number. It runs the agents I already use.
It picks the right agent for each request. It listens, keeps answers short, asks before it acts, and calls back when there's news.
Here's tonight. I'm in a car to the airport, and my phone rings.
Hi Vignesh, it's {{product}}. Claude Code needs a decision. Refunds use the same code as checkout. Should it fix them too?
Yes, but don't merge. While I have you, what's the latest from Northwind in Slack?
Their CTO, Maria, joined the shared channel an hour ago. She wants to see refunds in tomorrow's demo.
One more thing. Gemini saw your flight is delayed ninety minutes, so you'll miss dinner with Dana at seven. Should I move it to breakfast at eight?
I hang up. Claude Code keeps working.
Hi Vignesh. Claude Code is done. Checkout and refunds both pass, all two hundred fourteen tests. The pull request is open, not merged. The link is in your texts. Good luck with Northwind.
Three agents, one call. I never opened my laptop.
